method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the applicant (an individual bringing a claim or application to QCAT), with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; dates in one module, the rules and the exported questions in another, worked cases in a third; four regulative rules (asking a decision-maker for reasons, applying for review, asking the tribunal for written reasons, filing an appeal or application for leave) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Queensland Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2009 (Qld), act-2009-023, the version in force from 2026-10-22 (current on 2026-11-06), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2009-023.txt (text sha256 4acebadcf0a585572d04f8d762ee0d9f27aac6be5816725be3460a29acd41ca2), converted from the Queensland Legislation HTML view; with the 12 years of the Limitation of Actions Act 1974 s 10(4), which s 130 applies

seat: the applicant: an individual who brings a claim or application to the Queensland Civil and Administrative Tribunal (a minor civil dispute, another original-jurisdiction application, or a review of a government decision) and may later enforce, renew, reopen or appeal its decision (qcat-applicant.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run qcat-dates.l4 ; l4 run qcat-applicant.l4 ; l4 run qcat-cases-applicant.l4
checks.result: 222 assertions written, 222 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The provisions an applicant meets: ss 11, 11A, 12, 13(3)-(5), 14 and the schedule 3 definitions (minor civil disputes); ss 158, 159 (reasons for a reviewable decision); ss 33, 35, 36, 37, 38, 61 (starting; time); s 43 (representation); ss 46, 49 (withdrawing, starting again); ss 50, 50A (default decisions); ss 84-89 (settlement); ss 100-103, 107, 109 (costs, security); ss 122, 127 (reasons for the tribunal's decision); ss 129-134 (enforcement, s 130 with the Limitation of Actions Act 1974 s 10(4), renewal); ss 136-141 (reopening); ss 22, 51A, 138A, 145, 152 (operation pending challenge); ss 142, 143, 149-151 (appeals). Out: the tribunal's procedural powers, conferences, mediation, hearings, evidence, assessors, how appeals are decided, chapters 4-10 (establishment, members, registry, offences, rules, transitional) and schedules 1-2. Reasons in NOTES.md.
